change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: canManage() gives realm-wide group manage to holders of a VIEW-only all-groups permission
findings.body: `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so an all-groups permission that grants only `view` makes it return true. `GroupsResource.java:181` gates top-level group creation and moves with `auth.groups().requireManage()`. A V2 admin who was given only view on all groups can therefore create and re-parent top-level groups. The interface javadoc (GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:73-77) repeats this behaviour. `testManageAllGroups` only grants MANAGE, so the tests don't catch it. Fix: check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` here, and add a test where a VIEW-only all-groups permission gets 403 on group creation.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs, not group IDs, and never finds per-group resources
findings.body:
`findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` only matches resources whose type is `Groups`. Only the all-groups resource gets that type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:274). Per-group resources are created by name only, with no type set (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121). The loop then passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission`, which looks it up by name and falls back to the type resource. It adds the *resource* ID to `granted`, where ClientPermissionsV2.java:140 adds `resource.getName()`.

What this breaks:
- A per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant is never returned, so `UsersResource.getUsersCount` (UsersResource.java:398/425/430) returns a count from an empty group set, while the list endpoint shows the user through per-user `canView`. The count disagrees with the list and nothing reports an error.
- With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant, the set holds the type-resource ID. `searchForUser` (UsersResource.java:448-451, BruteForceUsersResource.java:147-150) puts that ID in `UserModel.GROUPS`, which filters the search to members of a group that doesn't exist, so the list comes back empty.

Fix: collect the IDs of groups that are actually granted (resource name = group id), and handle the all-groups grant separately, for example by returning empty and letting per-user evaluation decide.

findings.title: Does group deletion break when both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and _V2 are enabled?
findings.body: The listener is registered when V1 is enabled. `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` when V2 is enabled (lines 66-70), so a GroupRemovedEvent now reaches `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws UnsupportedOperationException (GroupPermissionsV2.java:173-175). Deleting a group would then fail. Can the two features be enabled together? If so, the listener should skip V2.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc names the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but GroupPermissions.java:376-379 checks `canManageMembers(group)`.

findings.title: Group-member visibility tests don't check users/count
findings.body: These tests pass because `toRepresentation` evaluates `canView` per user. They never call `users().count()`, which depends on `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` and is wrong for V2 (see the finding on GroupPermissionsV2.java:121). Asserting the count would catch that.

contracts.action: V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission feeds UserModel.GROUPS search filter and user count
contracts.before_after: Sibling adds resource names (object ids); new code adds resource ids and only finds the typed all-groups resource
contracts.visible_effect: Wrong users/count; empty user list under all-groups view-members grant

contracts.action: V2 groups().requireManage() for top-level group creation

summary: The new V2 group permissions have one security blocker: a view-only all-groups grant passes `canManage()`, and that check gates top-level group creation. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is also wrong. It returns resource IDs, and it never sees per-group resources because they have no type set. As a result `users/count` is wrong for admins who get user visibility through group grants, and an all-groups view-members grant makes the user list come back empty.
